subtype: Approach: telling the teacher when the friend will not stop [Revision]
passage: I am Shreya, and on Monday I saw Kabir on the stairs looking as if he had swallowed a stone. He had said no to his friend Salma twice about copying in the annual exam, and then he heard that Salma planned to bring a chit inside a pencil box. At break he walked to the staffroom door and asked his teacher Ms Iyer if he could talk to her alone. He was in there for five minutes. When he came out his face was red, and he said only, "I am not sure that was right, but it would have been worse." I do not know how he feels about Salma now, and I did not ask.

qa.q: Where did Salma plan to hide the chit?
qa.a: Salma planned to bring it inside a pencil box.

qa.q: How did Kabir seem to feel after speaking to Ms Iyer?
qa.a: Uneasy but resolved, since his face was red and he said he was not sure it was right but that it would have been worse.

qa.q: What other step could Kabir add for his friendship with Salma?
qa.a: He could tell Salma honestly why he spoke up and offer to help Salma study, because it shows he acted out of concern.

qa.q: How might Ms Iyer see Kabir coming to her?
qa.a: As a serious step, since he asked to talk alone and stayed five minutes, and she can now deal with a problem before the exam.

grounding: After refusing twice, a boy learns the friend plans a chit and tells the teacher privately, judging it worth stopping the bigger problem.

subtype: Approach: telling the teacher when the friend will not stop [Revision]
passage:
Monday: Akash asked Pankaj to let him copy in Wednesday's exam. Pankaj said no.
Tuesday: Akash asked again at the bus stop. Pankaj said no again. Then Akash showed him a folded chit tucked in his sock, covered in tiny formulas. "Fine. I'll manage myself." Pankaj's mouth went dry. He thought about it all evening: if Akash was caught, it would be far worse than a low mark; if he wasn't, he'd keep doing it. "Telling isn't about getting him in trouble," Pankaj decided. "It's about stopping something bigger."
Wednesday: Before the exam, Pankaj asked Mr Bhatt for a word in the corridor and told him quietly. Mr Bhatt thanked him and said he'd handle it without naming him. As the exam began, Mr Bhatt asked everyone to empty their pockets and socks onto their desks. Akash went pale, and the chit went into the bin.

qa.q: Where had Akash hidden the chit?
How did Pankaj feel when he saw the chit?
qa.a: Nervous and worried; his mouth went dry.
Telling Mr Bhatt privately before the exam, because it stopped the cheating without a public scene or naming Akash.

qa.q: What was the exam like for Akash?
qa.a: He went pale and had to throw the chit away, stopped before he could be caught using it.

grounding: After refusing twice, a boy learns his friend plans to bring a chit into the exam and quietly tells the teacher to stop a bigger problem.

subtype: Approach: telling the teacher when the friend will not stop [Revision]
passage: Suraj, you're asking whether telling a teacher makes you a tell-tale? Let me tell you something from my school days. My friend Mukul asked to copy from me before the final exam. I said no. He asked again. No. Then, the day before, he showed me the formulas he'd written on the inside of his wrist, under his watch strap. I, Varun, lay awake that night. If he was caught in the finals, it could cost him the whole year. I decided that keeping quiet was not being a good friend. So in the morning I spoke quietly to our class teacher. She thanked me, and before the paper she asked everyone to put their watches on the front desk. Mukul was angry with me for a month. Then he wasn't. Years later, he thanked me.

qa.q: Where had Mukul written the formulas?
qa.a: On the inside of his wrist, under his watch strap.

qa.q: How did young Varun feel that night?
qa.a: Worried and torn, lying awake over what to do.

qa.q: Which choice inside the story made the difference?
qa.a: Speaking quietly to the teacher before the paper, which stopped a much bigger problem for Mukul.

qa.q: How did Mukul feel about it over time?
qa.a: Angry for a month, then not, and years later grateful.

grounding: An elder recalls refusing a friend twice, then telling the teacher about his hidden formulas to prevent a bigger problem.
